story_title: As a ConnectSphere user, I want the interface to show me only the navigation, screens and actions appropriate to my role so that I can't see or reach functionality I'm not authorised for

acceptance_criteria.text: Given my role, when I view the main navigation, then only the nav items defined for my role are shown (e.g. an Attendee sees Browse Events and My Registrations, not Review Queue, Venues, or Assignments).
Given my role, when I open an event's detail page, then only the tabs permitted for my role are rendered (e.g. an Attendee sees only Overview; Venue Staff sees only Overview and Venue).
Given an action is not permitted for my role, when the relevant screen renders, then the corresponding button, link or tab is not shown at all, rather than shown disabled.
Given I navigate directly to a URL for a screen outside my role's permissions, when the page loads, then I see an access-denied state or am redirected, and no restricted data is rendered.

Given fields are restricted to internal roles (e.g. coordinator assignment, rejection reasons, venue/equipment arrangements), when an Attendee views an event, then those fields are absent from the page, not merely blank.
Given the Operations Manager role, when they use the interface, then they see the Assignments and All Events navigation matching their permissions.

test_cases.title: An Attendee's sidebar offers only the Attendee screens
test_cases.preconditions: Demo data is seeded. Logged in as Daniel Lim (daniel.lim@example.com / password123), an Attendee.
steps: Read every item in the left sidebar from top to bottom
test_cases.expected_result:
The sidebar reads exactly: Dashboard, Browse Events, My Registrations, Notifications.
Review Queue, Venues, Equipment, Booking Requests and Assignments do not appear anywhere in the sidebar.

test_cases.title: An Event Coordinator's sidebar offers the coordinator's working screens
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), an Event Coordinator.
steps: Read every item in the left sidebar from top to bottom
test_cases.expected_result:
The sidebar reads exactly: Dashboard, Review Queue, All Events, Venues, Equipment, Notifications.
Assignments, Booking Requests, Browse Events and My Registrations do not appear.

test_cases.title: Venue Staff and Technical Support get different sidebars from each other
test_cases.preconditions: Demo data is seeded. No one is signed in.
steps: Log in as marcus.wong@connectsphere.com with password123 and write down the sidebar
Log out, then log in as kenji.sato@connectsphere.com with password123
Write down the sidebar and compare the two
test_cases.test_data: Accounts: marcus.wong@connectsphere.com (Venue Staff), kenji.sato@connectsphere.com (Technical Support); Password: password123
test_cases.expected_result:
Marcus Wong's sidebar reads: Dashboard, Venues, Booking Requests, Notifications.
Kenji Sato's sidebar reads: Dashboard, Equipment, Equipment Requests, Notifications.
Neither sidebar contains the other's working screens, and the page layout and styling are identical for both.

test_cases.title: An Attendee opening an event sees only the Overview tab
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Lim (daniel.lim@example.com / password123), an Attendee. At least one confirmed event that is open for registration exists.
steps: Open the events list from the sidebar
Open the first event in the list
Read the row of tabs beneath the event title
test_cases.expected_result:
Only an Overview tab is shown.
No Equipment, Venue, Discussion, Attendees, Readiness or History tab appears — not even greyed out.

test_cases.title: An Event Coordinator opening an event sees the Overview and Equipment tabs
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), an Event Coordinator, with at least one event visible in All Events.
steps: Open All Events from the sidebar
Open the first event in the list
Read the row of tabs beneath the event title
test_cases.expected_result:
Both an Overview tab and an Equipment tab are shown, and clicking Equipment opens the equipment requirements for that event.
Discussion, Venue, Attendees, Readiness and History are not shown, because those screens are not built yet — a tab that leads nowhere is left out rather than shown broken.

test_cases.title: Venue Staff opening an event sees only the tabs that exist for them
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Marcus Wong (marcus.wong@connectsphere.com / password123), Venue Staff, viewing an event Venue Staff is allowed to see.
steps: Open an event from the events list
Read the row of tabs beneath the event title
test_cases.expected_result:
Only an Overview tab is shown.
No Equipment tab appears, because Venue Staff are not permitted it.
(AC2 names Venue and Overview for this role. The Venue tab is permitted but its screen is not built yet, so it is left out — see open question 1.)

test_cases.title: A Coordinator sees no Add venue control on the venue catalogue
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), an Event Coordinator, who may read the venue catalogue but not change it.
steps: Open Venues from the sidebar
Wait for the venue list to finish loading
Look for an Add venue button anywhere on the page
test_cases.expected_result:
The venue list is shown in full and is readable.
There is no Add venue button at all — not a greyed-out one, and not one that shows a message when clicked.
Clicking a venue row does not open an editor.

test_cases.title: Venue Staff do get the Add venue control on the same screen
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Marcus Wong (marcus.wong@connectsphere.com / password123), Venue Staff, who hold venue management.
steps: Open Venues from the sidebar
Wait for the venue list to finish loading
Look for an Add venue button
test_cases.expected_result:
An Add venue button is shown and is fully enabled, and clicking it opens the Add venue form.
This is the same screen as SPM-22-TC07, proving the control is added for the permitted role rather than hidden for everyone.

test_cases.title: Refusals are never expressed as a disabled control
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), an Event Coordinator.
steps: Open Venues from the sidebar and wait for it to load
Try to click every button and link on the page in turn
Note any control that appears greyed out, unclickable, or that does nothing when clicked
test_cases.expected_result:
Every control on the page responds when clicked.
No control is present-but-greyed-out as a way of saying the coordinator may not use it — controls they may not use are absent instead.

test_cases.title: The New event request action appears only for an Organiser
test_cases.preconditions: Demo data is seeded. No one is signed in.
steps: Log in as rachel.ng@meridianfina.com with password123 and look at the top right of the Dashboard
Log out, then log in as daniel.tan@connectsphere.com with password123
Look at the same place on the Dashboard
test_cases.test_data: Accounts: rachel.ng@meridianfina.com (Event Organiser), daniel.tan@connectsphere.com (Event Coordinator); Password: password123
test_cases.expected_result:
Rachel Ng's Dashboard shows a New event request button.
Daniel Tan's Dashboard shows no such button anywhere — it is absent, not disabled.

test_cases.title: An Attendee typing the Venues address is refused and sees no venue data
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Lim (daniel.lim@example.com / password123), an Attendee, whose sidebar does not offer Venues.
steps: Type the Venues page address directly into the browser address bar and press Enter
Wait for the page to finish loading
Read the whole page
test_cases.expected_result:
The page shows the heading Venues and a message 'You do not have access to this', explaining that the venue catalogue is for ConnectSphere staff, plus a Back to Dashboard button.
No venue name, building, capacity or opening hours appears anywhere on the page.

test_cases.title: An Operations Manager typing the Review Queue address is refused
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Grace Lim (grace.lim@connectsphere.com / password123), an Operations Manager. Reviewing requests belongs to the Event Coordinator.
steps: Type the Review Queue page address directly into the browser address bar and press Enter
Wait for the page to finish loading
test_cases.test_data: Account: grace.lim@connectsphere.com (Operations Manager); Page requested: Review Queue
test_cases.expected_result:
The page shows 'You do not have access to this' with the explanation that reviewing event requests is the Event Coordinator's role, and a Back to Dashboard button.
No list of events awaiting review is shown.
The browser does not show a 404 'page could not be found' error.

test_cases.title: A Coordinator typing the New event request address is refused at the door
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), an Event Coordinator. Only an Organiser may raise an event request.
steps: Type the New event request page address directly into the browser address bar and press Enter
Wait for the page to finish loading
test_cases.test_data: Account: daniel.tan@connectsphere.com (Event Coordinator); Page requested: New event request
test_cases.expected_result:
The page shows 'You do not have access to this' explaining that only an Event Organiser can raise an event request.
The event request form — Event name, Type of event, Purpose, Starts at, Ends at — is not rendered at all, so there is nothing to fill in and no Save draft button to press.

test_cases.title: An Attendee typing the Assignments address is refused
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Lim (daniel.lim@example.com / password123), an Attendee.
steps: Type the Assignments page address directly into the browser address bar and press Enter
Wait for the page to finish loading
test_cases.expected_result:
The page shows 'You do not have access to this' explaining that assigning coordinators is the Event Operations Manager's role.
No event awaiting assignment is listed.

test_cases.title: A signed-out visitor typing a restricted address is sent to log in
test_cases.preconditions: No one is signed in.
steps: Type the Venues page address directly into the browser address bar and press Enter
Wait for the page to finish loading
Log in as marcus.wong@connectsphere.com with password123
test_cases.test_data: Page requested: Venues, with no session; Account used afterwards: marcus.wong@connectsphere.com
test_cases.expected_result:
The browser lands on the Log in page showing 'Your session expired. Log in to continue where you left off.'
No venue data is shown before logging in.
After logging in as Venue Staff, the browser opens the Venues page that was originally asked for.

test_cases.title: A permitted role opening a screen that is not built yet is told so, not shown a 404
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Grace Lim (grace.lim@connectsphere.com / password123), an Operations Manager, whose sidebar offers Assignments.
steps: Click Assignments in the sidebar
Wait for the page to finish loading
Read the whole page
test_cases.expected_result:
The page is headed Assignments and explains that it will show submitted events waiting to be assigned to a coordinator.
A notice reads 'This screen is not built yet', naming S-28 (Coordinator Assignment) and confirming the role does have access.
The browser does not show a 404 'page could not be found' error.

test_cases.title: Internal planning fields are absent from an Attendee's view of an event
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Lim (daniel.lim@example.com / password123), an Attendee. A confirmed event that is open for registration exists and has a coordinator assigned, an expected attendance and special requirements recorded.
steps: Open the events list from the sidebar
Open the first event in the list
Read every label and value shown on the page from top to bottom
test_cases.expected_result:
The page shows the event's title, description, category, dates and status, and what is needed to register.
There is no Coordinator row, no Organiser row, no Expected attendance row, no Special requirements row, no Rejection reason row and no venue or equipment arrangements.
Those labels are absent entirely — the page does not show them with an empty value or a dash.

test_cases.title: The same event shows its internal fields to a Coordinator
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), an Event Coordinator, opening the same event used in SPM-22-TC17.
steps: Open All Events from the sidebar
Open the same event used in SPM-22-TC17
Read every label and value shown on the page
test_cases.test_data: Account: daniel.tan@connectsphere.com (Event Coordinator); the event opened in SPM-22-TC17
test_cases.expected_result:
The Coordinator and Organiser rows are both shown with names, and Expected attendance is shown with its number.
This confirms that the rows missing in SPM-22-TC17 are withheld from the Attendee rather than simply not recorded on that event.

test_cases.title: The Operations Manager's navigation matches their permissions
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Grace Lim (grace.lim@connectsphere.com / password123), an Operations Manager.
steps: Read every item in the left sidebar from top to bottom
Read the role shown beneath the name in the top bar
test_cases.expected_result:
The sidebar reads exactly: Dashboard, Assignments, All Events, Notifications.
The top bar shows Grace Lim with 'Operations Manager' beneath the name.
Review Queue, Venues, Equipment and Booking Requests do not appear, because assigning coordinators and overseeing events is what this role does.

test_cases.title: Every item in the Operations Manager's sidebar opens without an error
test_cases.preconditions: Logged in as Grace Lim (grace.lim@connectsphere.com / password123), an Operations Manager.
steps: Click Dashboard and wait for it to load
Click Assignments and wait for it to load
Click All Events and wait for it to load
Click Notifications and wait for it to load
test_cases.expected_result:
All four screens open. None shows a 404 'page could not be found' error and none shows an access-denied message.
Assignments and Notifications explain that they are not built yet; Dashboard and All Events show their real content.

open_questions: AC2 says Venue Staff see Overview and Venue, but the Venue tab has no screen behind it yet (IMPLEMENTED_TABS in src/lib/eventTabs.ts limits the tab bar to Overview and Equipment). Venue Staff therefore see Overview alone today, which SPM-22-TC06 records. Is leaving an unbuilt-but-permitted tab out the behaviour you want, or should the tab appear and lead to a 'not built yet' screen the way the sidebar items now do?

SPM-22 added seven placeholder screens (Review Queue, Assignments, Equipment, Equipment Requests, Booking Requests, Browse Events, My Registrations) plus Notifications, so that every sidebar item leads somewhere and AC4 can be tested on all of them. Each is permission-guarded first and empty second. Confirm this is the intended approach — the alternative was to hide sidebar items whose screens do not exist, which would have removed Assignments from the Operations Manager's sidebar and contradicted AC6.

AC3 was verified on the venue catalogue, which is the only screen today that renders the same route to two roles with different permissions. Once the review queue, booking and equipment screens are real, AC3 deserves a case on each of them; as written it can only be checked where a permitted and a refused role share a screen.

Two database migrations on this branch (add_event_seed_key and add_event_sequence_number) are not applied to the shared database, so the events list returns an error and no event can be opened. SPM-22-TC04, TC05, TC06, TC17 and TC18 cannot be executed until someone applies them with prisma migrate deploy using the direct (non-pooled) connection string.
